data.jobspec:
#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   --job-name=copy_methane4
#   --ntasks=1
#   --mem=1gb
#   --time=24:05:00
#   --output=parallel_%j.log

#flux: --job-name=copy_methane4
#flux: -n 1
#flux: --time-limit=24h5m

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem=1gb
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on nodes with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted Slurm option: --output=parallel_%j.log
# Slurm's %j token (job id) is not portable in Flux output directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose a unique filename.

. /home/rs/anaconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate mosdef-study38

rsync -av /home/rs/space/projects/final_repro_methane/reproducibility_study/reproducibility_project/methane_systemsize_subproject4/* .

reasons: The original Slurm job requested 1GB of memory (`--mem=1gb`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this can under-provision the job and risk OOM or degraded performance.
